title: Ferrari Avocado Bowling Alley
description: A Ferrari sits at one end of a long flat surface acting as a bowling lane. The user configures the car's launch velocity, steering angle, and spin, then releases it to knock down a triangular formation of ten oversized avocados arranged as bowling pins. Physics-based collision, friction, and restitution govern the outcome, and the user must knock down all pins across multiple attempts while tuning parameters.
prompt: Create a single HTML file using Three.js r170 with GLTFLoader and OrbitControls from CDN. Load shared_assets/ferrari.glb as the bowling ball vehicle and shared_assets/Avocado.glb ten times arranged in a standard triangular bowling pin formation at the far end of a 60-unit-long rectangular lane. Scale the Ferrari to roughly 1.5 units wide and each Avocado to about 1 unit tall. Implement a simple custom physics engine (no external library) supporting velocity integration, AABB collision detection, friction (coefficient 0.3), and restitution (coefficient 0.4). Each avocado pin has mass 1 and the Ferrari has mass 5. Add a ground plane textured as a wooden lane with gutter boundaries. Camera starts behind the Ferrari looking down the lane; use OrbitControls. Add ambient light intensity 0.6 and a directional light casting shadows. Create an HTML control panel overlay with: (1) a velocity slider 5-30 m/s, (2) a steering angle slider from -15 to +15 degrees, (3) a spin slider from -5 to 5 rad/s applied as angular velocity around the car's up axis, (4) a Launch button, (5) a Reset button to restore all pins and car position, and (6) a scoreboard showing pins knocked down out of 10. When Launch is clicked, validate that velocity is between 5-30, angle is within range, and spin is within range; if invalid show an alert. Apply the velocity vector in the lane direction rotated by the steering angle, and apply spin as continuous yaw rotation during travel. On each frame, integrate positions, apply friction deceleration, detect collisions between the Ferrari and each avocado using bounding spheres, and on collision transfer momentum causing avocados to topple by rotating them 90 degrees over 0.5 seconds and sliding them. An avocado counts as knocked down if it has rotated more than 45 degrees from upright. Update the scoreboard in real time. After the car stops or exits the lane, display a result message. The user should need 6-10 interaction steps across multiple launches with different parameter combinations to achieve a perfect strike of all ten pins.
